name: Galphimia glauca
short: In a trial against lorazepam, 11 patients (group not stated) withdrew for adverse reactions; tolerability did not differ. Cited trials had no placebo group. Mouse data suggest haloperidol interaction.
text: The two human trials cited here compared Galphimia glauca extract with anti-anxiety medicines, not with placebo. In a 15-week double-blind trial against lorazepam in generalised anxiety disorder (12 weeks of treatment plus 3 withdrawal weeks), 191 patients started and 104 finished; the tolerability analysis, which included 11 patients who withdrew because of adverse reactions (the abstract does not say from which group or what the reactions were), showed no difference between treatments, and no cases of tolerance, intoxication, dependence or "suppression syndrome" were recorded. In a 10-week trial in 167 patients, daytime sleepiness was found in 4.7% of those given the extract compared with 22.2% of those given alprazolam. Toxicology data are from animals and cell tests: in mice given standardised extracts by mouth for 28 days there were no deaths and no organ changes on histopathology, only reduced spontaneous activity, and liver function measures were unchanged after 56 days; in vitro tests showed no genotoxic effect. On interactions, the only cited evidence is a mouse study in which the extract and its galphimines potentiated the cataleptic effect of the antipsychotic haloperidol; no human interaction data were found in the cited sources.
